meta.title: Engine source data — stat model, K values, caps, loot model, craft prices

combat_arena.range_note: Legacy centre-to-centre table kept for older readers. Ordinary and player basics resolve through `normal_attack.profiles`; a profile declares whether its metres are centre distance or the gap between body edges.

normal_attack.note: Ordinary basics. The legacy adapter maps the spawn line to a profile and the player mapping maps its weapon group to one; neither delivery nor reach is guessed from the sprite or the line elsewhere. A body-edge profile measures the gap between footprints, so 0.20 m with two 0.25 m bodies reaches at a 0.70 m centre distance and stops at 0.65 m. A centre profile keeps its authored centre distance. Stand-off bodies release a non-homing single-target shot at the attack beat; a ready strike replaces that opportunity and the shot is not a second damage stream.

combat_arena.note: Transient forest combat presentation selected by the battlefield-style setting. Ground units, units per second, and attack profiles that state their range basis; bodies keep their footprint edges apart and melee bodies claim reachable contact points inside their stop band. No obstacles, obstacle navigation, positional evasion or networked play. Damage, clocks, statuses and rewards still use the existing combat pipeline. Classic combat and offline progress do not read this section.

stat.note: Stats are SPENT, not granted (owner ruling). `per_level` is gone: a level grants 5 stat points (2 in Paragon, levels 101-190), and `stat = base + points x point_value`. The tree's own points are the tree's business: its budget and the rate a level pays live in `tools/data/tree.json` (`points.currencies.tree`), and the level curve grants two of them a level, so a level-cap character holds 381 points against a tree that is deliberately wider than that budget - the ranks are not what the level cap grants. The player allocates freely, mid-combat, and Respec is free but town-only. `statAt(level)` is no longer the player line - it is the REFERENCE even-split line (points/7), the build every published number and mob_HP is priced against; the focused max (all points and all 13 items in one stat) is the ceiling, printed beside it. `per_level` survives only on the player reference ramp if re-added; the mob stat line is flat (mob.stat).

crippled.note: Earth's status: the body is injured, so its direct hits and skill presses deal 20% less damage. It does not slow the attack clock or cooldowns, and it has no mob cooldown effect. No stacks: a second application refreshes the three seconds. The payoff row is Aftershock.

status.dot_cap_note: burn + poison + the earth line a row leaves (Sand Storm), combined, as a multiple of confirmed Element damage per second (elements.md section 6). burn reaches 1.0 at 5 stacks x 0.20 and poison reaches 1.0 at 10 stacks x 0.10; together they are still held at the shared 1.5 cap.
status.mob_side: decided — mob→player is unchanged (combat.md §5). Player→mob splits three ways: DoT (burn/poison/bleed) lands in full; damage-shaping debuffs (every curse, chill's Armour cut, crippled's outgoing-damage cut) land; control is bounded, never a lockout — mobs are immune to root/freeze/held-past-action and stun chance has no Cap, while a separate rolling stop-time budget (mob_control_budget_pct) limits total stopped time. Chill/shock speed cuts obey their own Caps, so no fight can be stun-locked. No mob resist stat. combat.md §5b

races.note: Fantasy taxonomy only: a Race groups related Species; a Species owns its own gameplay rules and may author any number of Variants. Race membership does not grant mechanics. Empty Races are allowed as spaces for future world content.

mob.note: Family > Species > Variant: Family is a broad fantasy grouping, Species is an individual creature lineage, and each Species may own any number of named level Variants. Body classes remain the four card sizes. Innate Element stays a separate spawn roll (world.md).
mob.stat_block: `mob.forms` holds optional named field forms for real zone bands. Each Species may author as many fixed-level Variants as the fantasy content needs; the zone midpoint selects the Variant's name, live combat Core, optional damage override and drop identity, while `zone_levels[zoneId]` supplies its actual fixed spawn level. A Variant inherits its Species' default damage type unless it overrides it. Forms are optional field labels and legacy projections; runtime normal and Elite spawns read the selected Variant Core and damage type plus the authored Species zone level. No Core line or level scales at runtime.
mob.power_note: A mob's damage per second is its own power over the zone mean, times the published mob_PS(L) curve: power = mob.species[].power_base + K_MOB_PS_STAT × (wPhys × Str + wMagic × Int), where [wPhys, wMagic] comes from the selected Variant damage override or its Species default. The same split mob.damage_split spends divides the hit. The zone's average mob is the published curve — each Species multiplier is read against that same zone mean, so the average is 1 by construction and no gate re-checks it, so the species term only moves the mobs actually in front of the player and no zone edge, timeline, ladder or survival number changes. `power_base` is the per-species Base knob - 1.00 is neutral, and raising or lowering it tilts a species without touching its stat vector.

attack_clock_per_sec.note: combat.md section 1: a normal and an elite mob swing once a second, a boss 0.8 times. The mob clock is capped at 1 / caps.attack_interval_sec, the same clock rule the player obeys, so no Crippled stack or future mob speed line can out-run the game's one attack ceiling.

curve.note: The passive tree exists (tools/data/tree.json: three connected branches, 64 nodes) and has no effect on this line (owner ruling): it is deliberately not folded in, and the published rates are the empty-tree baseline. mob_HP(L) is a static published table, never priced from player DPS: every zone edge carries its own HP (mob.zones[].hp) plus one cap anchor at the level cap, and every level between is linearly interpolated. typical_gear_DPS(L) is read back out of that table, never priced into it, and mob_PS(L) = typical_gear_DPS(L) / mob_damage_divisor. Above the level-90 edge the read-back line runs to the cap anchor (tools/lib/engine.ts mobHpAt - X37).

extend.rule: mob_HP(L) = stat_c(L) x skill(L) x gear_factor for every zone edge above `from_level`. The gear factor is the one already measured at the level-90 published edge and then held flat: gear stops improving while levels do not, so HP past zone 9 rises on the stat line and the skill multiplier alone. Zones 1-9 keep their published anchors untouched — this only computes the edges that did not exist. Seeding from the last published edge is what keeps the line continuous, and it lands the zone-18 edge within a fraction of a percent of the owner projection.

damage_split.note: A Variant may override its Species' default damage type; the selected tag divides its hit: physical is entirely the armour-able half, magic is entirely the Element-resistible half, mixed is 50/50. This makes the tag a rule instead of decoration: the right Core attribute drives power and the hit meets the matching defence.

reach.rules: A group is a queue ordered front line first. A weapon's reach is how many queue slots it may hit: 1 = the front slot only, 2 = front and second, 3 = any slot in the group. Only the front slot swings at the player; a stand-off mob shoots or casts from where it stands and still counts inside the 3-attacker cap. If the front slot dies while stand-off mobs live, a reach-1 attack waits one engage cycle (1 sec) for the group to close; reach 2 and 3 keep pressing. AoE keeps its damage rules (60% per target · Cap 3) and only changes which 3: melee fans from the front, stand-off picks any 3; its Mana price does not change with target count. There are no tiles, no movement speed and no coordinates — reach is the whole positional model, and it replaces the stray 'within 3 tiles' wording.

spawn_weights.note: how often each farming body shows up in a group. Every zone spends its encounter budget once: the published mob_HP(L) curve is the zone AVERAGE mob, so each group entry divides its body multiplier by the weighted average of the bodies that zone can field. A Large mob is tougher and rarer, a Small mob cheaper and common, and the drop line, the stone funnel and the timeline never move.

mob.level_rule: a mob spawns at the attacking player's level clamped into its zone's range, so mob_HP is read at that level between the two ends printed in mob-roster.md (checks.md D1), and a player past a zone's last level keeps fighting that zone at its own edge.

sizes.name: Boss
sizes.reads_as_note: A boss is not a size, it is a species that happens to be huge: it declares which of the three body classes a weapon's `size_mult` reads it as (- HugePatch section 12). Default Large; a boss may override it on its own entry.

elite.name: Elite
elite.note: Elite is a rarity flag, not a fifth size: an Elite is always forced to the Large body and carries its own numbers, so no two multipliers ever stack. What an Elite pays in Tier stones is the key `loot.elite_tier_stones` — an expected count per kill, folded into `tierStonesPerHr` — named here rather than retyped.

size_rules: Four card sizes, copied from Ragnarok: Small · Medium · Large · Boss. A size REPLACES the base numbers, it never multiplies with Elite or with another size.

Small and Medium form the groups world.md counts (1-2 / 2-3 / 3-5). Large, Elite and Boss always appear alone. Each species carries only the sizes that fit it; every species with normal variants needs Small or Medium to enter a group, while Large remains the solo Elite body.

The body class carries a base Evasion as a percent on top of its species Dex line: Small +20%, Medium +10%, and nothing above Medium - a Large, Elite or Boss body is not punished for its size, it simply presents all of itself. The rating under the percent is the mob's own flat Core attribute line (`mob.stat`), never a level number.
Body classes do not scale damage: Small, Medium and Large share the same base PS, so pack size is what sets them apart - Small and Medium come in groups while Large stands alone.

species_rules: A species is a MULTIPLY vector on the same stat block a player has, so the zone's average mob stays on the published HP anchor. Check X19 fails any species whose multipliers do not average 1.00.

accuracy_mult scales mob accuracy on top of the shared K values. This is what makes the Evasion Cap 80 question answerable: Cap 80 is reachable against the lowest-accuracy species (Slime) and close to worthless against the highest ones (Wolf · Elf · Dragon), so no single mob accuracy number can close C1 - the species mix does.
innate Element is rolled on spawn and is NOT part of the species. element_bias only tilts the roll inside the zone's own 1-2 Elements, so players still have to prepare res in advance (world.md).

A species that carries a weapon is the only kind a weapon-slot piece can come from; every species still drops from the non-weapon slots, so the 8% base drop rate and the loot.md funnel are untouched by this flag. Slime · Spider · Dryad are the weaponless lineages, which is why goblin (zone 1) is where the weapon part of the drop table starts.

A Species has at least one named fixed-level Variant; it may author as many as its fantasy content needs. Bands are valid and non-overlapping, gaps carry the nearest earlier Variant, and higher zones keep the final Variant and field label.

A species may appear only where its `habitat` allows. `habitat` is the region list it may live in (the geography layer the zone `region` names) and `zones` is where it currently does, so `zones` must be a subset of the regions those zones carry. Re-placing a species is a `habitat`/`zones` data edit, never a roster rewrite, and it moves no price.
Mob Evasion uses the selected variant's authored Core Dex, with the body base percent on top. The field form remains a label projection; Core is authored data, not scaled at runtime.

`mob.races` is the broad taxonomy; `mob.species[].race` assigns each Species to one Race. `mob.variants` holds any number of authored level Variants per Species. `mob.forms` is the optional field-label projection; missing labels inherit the latest earlier form. Each subzone has an independent Species spawn pool, pools may overlap across environments, and their union covers the zone cast. Levels 101-180 remain playable and reuse the final Variant and available label. Variant rarity and lean remain Variant-owned. Mob plates use the Species icon; Elite/Boss remain rank overlays.

A proposed zone layout that re-zones the world is a new world, not a mob pass: the zone set is the shipped eighteen with its place regions, and where a Species lives is a habitat-legal data edit. New Races may be declared without members; adding a Species or Variant does not require matching a roster count. A subzone carries one of its zone's own Elements, never a new one.

A species' trait is a mechanic, not a label: `mob.species[].mechanics` names flag keys from the closed set `mob.trait_mechanics.set`, and the client runs each one - a body that cannot bleed, a body that bursts poison when it dies, or a body that swings faster at the same damage per second. A species with no `mechanics` row is an ordinary body. Resistance and weakness are separate Species profile fields, not traits.

A species' trait is a mechanic, not a label: `mob.species[].mechanics` names flag keys from the closed set `mob.trait_mechanics.set`, and the client runs each one - a body that cannot bleed, a body that bursts poison when it dies, or a body that swings faster at the same damage per second. A species with no `mechanics` row is an ordinary body. Resistance and weakness are separate Species profile fields, not traits.

stat.note: Each fixed-level Species Variant owns one authored integer Core block (`mob.variants[species][variant].core`): its role name guides the Str/Agi/Vit/Int/Lck allocation while Dex follows `mob.core_spend.dex_cap` and the body’s Agi identity, so a level band never turns into a Dex-only climb. Runtime normal and Elite spawns use that Variant Core without scaling. Zone forms keep optional field labels; mobs have no equipment or passive tree.

core_spend.note: One integer Core point block for every body. Dex is capped per Variant band, and the cap bends down for a low-Agi body, so a level band no longer carries a Dex-only climb. Wis stays 0 (no mob line reads it), physical Int stays 0 (no magic power), every live stat carries points, and a magic profile keeps Int above Str. Bosses and Uniques keep their source Species Vit.

field_labels.note: An active field label uses its assigned form name when present; missing labels inherit the latest form and levels 101-180 stay on the last available form. Elite and Boss are ranks over that name. Drop Variants remain Species-owned loot identities. Colour is a client concern - the data carries no hex value.

mob.variant_drops_note: Each Species may author any number of Variants; every Variant name owns its base junk item, rarity and lean in this table. A Species may provide one additional junk item in any subset of rarities. `lean` is the collectible stream a Variant tilts toward, applied through leanReweight so the total expected drops/kill is conserved; its Species race has no automatic effect on the drop. `none` is the identity, used by Unique and Boss drops that already pay their own stone lines. Rarity is free by construction - every rarity's chance is the junk line divided by its own sell price - so moving a Variant between rarities never moves reference base gold/kill; realised income uses town demand.

mob.resist_rules: Each Species authors one resistance line (`mob.species[].resistance`) and one weakness (`mob.species[].weakness`); its attack Element is a separate line. No Element counters another and no profile tilts the Vit line. Every other Element meets no resistance, and a weakness is a damage amplifier, never a resistance line. Bosses and Uniques inherit their Species profile. X54 checks one line each, declared Elements, a non-identical weak Element and the player Cap.
mob.skills_note: Mob skills are an optional kit from `tools/data/mob-skills.json`. Most species carry 0-2; bosses and uniques may carry up to 4. Resolution is override-only: unique > boss > variant > species, never a merge. A strike replaces the mob's next basic swing and deals exactly that swing's damage, so mob PS remains the sole DPS budget. Auras are passive, group-scoped defensive effects (engaged group, or the source's own line) and never add damage or speed. X55 validates the library, kits, refs, cap, element/status coverage and uniqueness.

trait_mechanics.note: A species' trait is read as a mechanic, not as a sentence. The set is closed: every key is a rule the client runs, and `mob.species[].mechanics` names which ones a lineage carries. None of them touches mob_HP, mob PS, the drop line or the stone funnel - the published anchors stay as they are. What changes is what a fight reads like: a body that cannot bleed, a body that bursts, or a body that swings faster.

bleed_immune.note: A body with no blood cannot bleed: the physical DoT never lands on it. Every other status lands as usual.

poison_burst.note: When the body bursts, the fighter takes a poison line worth this share of the dead mob's own damage per second. It is a guaranteed application, not a 20% proc - the pop is the whole body - and the fighter's own status immunity is the only answer to it.

fast_clock.note: Swings 1.25 times as often at the same damage per second: the hit is thinner by the same share, so the mob deals exactly its published PS. The one clock Cap the player obeys still binds.

spawn_packs.note: The body a normal spawn takes, tilted per sub-zone. `even` is the plain roll - every body the species can field at equal odds, exactly what a bare ground rolls. `swarm` doubles Small, `brute` doubles Medium. Each zone's three sides carry one of each, so the zone's average body mix - and the published mob_PS behind it - is unchanged; only one side reads cheaper and one reads heavier.

bleed.mitigations: none — bleed has no counter stat in the game and its DoT bypasses Energy Shield; healing can shorten the fight
bleed.mob_side: decided — bleed is a DoT, so it lands on mobs in full from our own bleed sources: the axe's `Chance to bleed %` line, and a press whose row grants the proc. It is a ROLLED status like an Element proc, so it passes the Alignment gate before its own chance (owner ruling) — the same gate a stun passes. The reverse is a mob skill: the high-Str physical lineages (Orc · Golem · Troll · Drake) inflict bleed as their signature, delivered as a DoT slice of their already-priced mob_PS, not extra power (combat.md §5b)
bleed.note: PoE bleed: physical damage over time, does not stack, a new application refreshes the duration, base duration 5 sec, base total 70% of the inflicting hit's physical damage, unaffected by armour, cannot crit. bleed_dps = K_BLEED x physical_per_hit / bleed_time_sec, so it does not scale with attack speed — slow heavy hits are the build. Delivered by the axe's `Chance to bleed %` line and by a press whose row grants the proc; no curse carries it.

level_gain.base_note: The flat base each pool starts from before its Core attribute is added (owner ruling): Max HP = hp_base + Vit x K_VIT_HP + level term · Max Mana = mana_base + Int x K_INT_MP + level term · weight capacity = weight_base + Str x K_STR_WEIGHT. A level-1 character (stat 12) reads 540 HP / 148 mana / 1,024 capacity, so the opening set - the sword at 35 and the junk frames at 230 - is carried untaxed.

xp.note: xp_to_next(L) = kills(L) × 10 × min(L, mob_level_cap) · kills(L) is the RAGNAROK curve: the classic base-EXP table of RO (1-99) applied in log space and rescaled so level 1 costs 20 kills and the completion checkpoint (level 100) lands on its published 63,231, with the last two steps set by the owner rule — the step INTO 100 is 1.5× the step into 99 in XP — so the cliff ends on one final push, which keeps RO's signature — a step at every 10-level boundary and a steeper final decade — at this game's scale. The anchors are one per level through the cliff (85-100) and at each boundary, so the steps survive interpolation. Past `plateau_from` (100, the completion level) the XP bar is FLAT and holds the XP of the step out of `plateau_step_at` (89 → 90, the last step before RO's own cliff): completing the 91-100 push lowers the bar, and the post-completion loop is a plateau the player paces, never a wall. The progression checkpoints derive from this curve in engine/index.ts (CHECKPOINTS_KILLS), so a re-shape moves the bands and the town budgets with it.

mod_weights.note: Effective drop weight of every Mod line = role weight x value(X) (equipment-slot-pools.md). tools/loot.ts is the only consumer and the weight table printed in equipment-slot-pools.md is generated from these rows, so a weight can never be typed twice. `weight` is one number, or [low, mid, high] for the early-game Flat group whose weight falls with Item quality.
mod_weights.flat_group_note: The 0.5 group is the early-game line: at level 10 it is 1/3 of power, at level 100 it is 1%. Drops full of Flat lines naturally stop being upgrades as the player moves up zones, which is what makes crafting the answer rather than luck (equipment-slot-pools.md). These four ids are also what F11 counts as a Flat line — Stat Mod flat, Evasion flat and the three Gear Mods are Flats by name but not part of this group.

rows.why: Element builds hunt repeats, so no reduction

rows.label: Elemental resistance Cap %
rows.why: the tree's own line (owner ruling): no Base frame offers it and the weight is 0, so the weighted pool pick can never draw it — the control branch's last node is the only source

rows.label: Accuracy %
rows.why: Cheap but lifts the 80% hit floor · frequent filler

rows.label: Stat Mod flat
rows.v100: +3.1% (on a maxed stat) · **+11.9%** (on an uninvested stat)
rows.why: Stat Mod flat rolls on every item, so an uninvested stat is always reachable — the single-stat half of the Stat Mod slot

rows.label: All stats flat
rows.v100: +96% of a fresh build's uninvested stat line, and it thins toward the flat ceiling as the stats fill
rows.why: A PoE-style all-attributes line: one roll lifts all seven Core attributes at once, so it is weighted rarer than the single-stat Stat Mod flat it shares the slot with

rows.label: Elemental alignment %
rows.why: Element builds only

rows.label: Cooldown reduction %
rows.why: Whole skill list is worth only +7.7% DPS (skill-pool.md) → CDR is truly a secondary line

rows.label: Max HP flat
rows.why: Dies off late-game · weight differs by quality tier (low 0.5 · mid 0.4 · high 0.25)

rows.label: Max Mana flat
rows.why: Matters only while the pool is still small

rows.label: Max Mana %
rows.v100: +16% of pool · auras **reserve a fixed %**, so a bigger pool leaves a bigger usable pool after reserving
rows.why: Cast builds channel longer · aura builds like this line

rows.label: Physical/Magic power flat
rows.why: Same as Max HP Flat — an early-game line

rows.label: Elemental power flat / %
rows.v100: ~21% of a hit after the Alignment gate
rows.why: Element builds required

rows.label: Armour / Evasion / Energy Shield flat
rows.why: The Gear Mod is the Base's own school line (item-base.md), so it rolls at Primary weight on the five armour slots; the three Gear Mod weights were missing before the loot sim and are set here

rows.label: Max Energy Shield %
rows.why: The Int build’s scaling defensive line, same shape as the Max HP % and Max Mana % it sits beside

rows.label: Energy Shield Regeneration %
rows.why: Amplifies the base ES regen (`energy_shield.regen_pct`) the way Life Regeneration % amplifies the Vit line — a rate line, never a pool line, so it cannot raise the shield's ceiling (checks.md X25)

rows.label: Life Regeneration %
rows.v100: +15% of the Vit-derived regen line · Vit 510 × 0.25 = 127.5/sec, so +19.1/sec and 13% off Push downtime
rows.why: Recovery, not a pool — it cannot raise the ceiling, so it is the defensive line that never breaks an HP Cap, and the only one that shortens the walk back to camp (checks.md D9)

rows.label: Mana Regeneration %
rows.v100: +25% of the Int-derived regen line · Int 510 × 0.28 = 142.8/sec, so +35.7/sec of cast sustain
rows.why: Mana is the real casting bottleneck as designed (skill-pool-system.md), so this buys uptime with the bar full rather than more damage per press

rows.label: All Resistance %
rows.v100: +11.1% EHP across every Element at once · 20% off the Elemental half of a 50/50 hit
rows.why: Weaker per Element than Elemental resistance % (top 20 vs 30) precisely because it covers all five, and it lands on the ring, amulet and cape slots that carry no resistance today — rarer by design

rows.label: Attack damage % / Spell damage %
rows.v100: a ladder multiplier, not a power line: it scales what the ladder already deals, so it is worth most on the build that finished that ladder
rows.why: The two rows are the same shape on opposite ladders, so they price together. Rarer than Attack speed and Accuracy because one line multiplies the whole finished press instead of one term inside it, and the pair never crosses: a caster has no use for the attack half and a melee build none for the spell half

rows.label: Elemental resistance Cap %
rows.v100: not a gear line: it lifts `caps.elem_res` toward `caps.elem_res_max` and only the passive tree grants it
rows.why: The weight is zero on purpose, and no Base frame names the line in its pool, so a drop can never carry the unlock — the row exists because every `mods.json` line resolves a weight (`weightOf` would otherwise read undefined). Tree cage T9 holds the zero and the empty pool.

rows.label: Armour %
rows.v100: +3.7 points of cut on a zone-9 physical half (41.7% -> 45.4% at full Str, no flat)
rows.why: A PoE ratio cuts less of a bigger number, so a % on Armour is a modest line by construction (X22 holds the cut inside 10-40%) — same rarity as Max HP %

rows.label: Evasion %
rows.v100: +2.2% evasion on the Dex line (105 -> 122 at Dex 210)
rows.why: Evasion is a rating fed straight into the entropy roll, so it scales cleanly where Armour does not

rows.label: Life Regeneration flat
rows.early: a level-1 build has 3/sec, so +31 more than doubles it
rows.why: Dies off late-game exactly like Max HP Flat — weight differs by quality tier (low 0.5 · mid 0.4 · high 0.25)

rows.label: Mana Regeneration flat
rows.why: Same early-game shape as Life Regeneration flat; the flat form carries the first zones where the % form has nothing to multiply

rows.label: Perfect dodge %
rows.v100: scales the Lck line, so it is worth most on a build that has not finished the line
rows.early: a level-1 Lck sits at under 1%, where +3% is a large multiplier on the chance
rows.why: The Cap binds near the top of the maxed Lck ratio, so this line is worth least on a maxed-Lck piece and decisive on a low one — the same shape as an % line on any other low rate. It is also defined but not offered: no Base pool in bases.json rolls it, so today it is a drop-weight row and nothing more.

rows.label: Status Alignment resistance %
rows.v100: cuts the 20% status proc to 15% and cuts crowd control (stun/stop) too — the gap between status applications goes 2.3 sec -> 3.3 sec
rows.early: same ratio, fewer absolute hits to proc on
rows.why: The status proc is 20% per landed hit and there is no other gear answer to it — or to the crowd control statuses carry — (Holy veil is a timed buff, not a line), so it carries a defensive line of its own; 0.7 matches the other "answers something niche" defensive rows

rows.label: Chance to bleed %
rows.v100: a second bleed source beside Lacerate's own 40% while the curse is up (formula-offense.md section 4)
rows.early: bleed is a fixed fraction of one physical hit, so the line is worth the same at every level - only the hit behind it grows
rows.why: A weapon-only line (one-handed and two-handed axes). It is the always-on answer to the bleed slot Lacerate already owns, so it prices like the other "answers something niche" rows; bleed is physical DoT with no Element tag and cannot crit, so the line adds reliability rather than a new multiplier

rows.label: Chance to stun %
rows.v100: adds to the uncapped lightning-Alignment stun chance; the Alignment gate still applies (elements.md section 6)
rows.early: stun is a fixed 1 sec stop, so the line is worth the same at every level
rows.why: A weapon-only line (mace). Stun chance has no Cap; Alignment remains the status gate, and the mob's separate rolling stop-time budget limits how much time a proc can remove from its clock

rows.label: Block chance %
rows.v100: the second avoidance layer: a blocked hit is deleted outright, the same shape as perfect dodge
rows.early: the Cap binds near the top of the shield's own ladder, so the line is worth most while the shield is still low
rows.why: Shield offhand only, and line 1 rather than a random roll, so the layer cannot spread onto every slot. Weighted like the other defensive answers; formula-defense.md prints the roll order and X43 proves the Cap is reachable from the shield alone

rows.label: Armour penetration %
rows.v100: cuts the mob's armour ratio, which only matters where the roster's armour is high enough to bite
rows.early: the first zones' armour is small, so the line reads as near-zero there and grows into its value
rows.why: Crossbow only, line 1. It is a cut on the mob-side armour ratio, not a new damage multiplier, so it prices against the armour it removes; the mob roster's armour column is what decides where it pays

energy_shield.note: Elemental resistance is a GEAR line (owner ruling): no Core attribute feeds it, so `K_MOB_RES` belongs to the mob stat vector alone and the player reads the resistance off the Mod rows. Energy Shield is fed by Wis flat (`K_WIS_ES`) with the gear lines riding on top (owner ruling): pool = (`Wis` x `K_WIS_ES` + `energy_shield_flat`) x (1 + `max_energy_shield_pct`/100). Regen is `regen_pct` (3) percent of the max pool per second once `delay_sec` (3) have passed without a hit, so the base rate alone returns the whole pool in 100 / `regen_pct` sec - the same full-pool span the mana pool was tuned to. Regen is amplified by an `es_regen` line from a skill, Mod or passive: rate x (1 + `es_regen`/100), and that is the only way it moves. The 3 sec delay is the owner's ruling: it puts the shield back inside a normal mob swing gap, so a caster who breaks contact recovers a tick before the next hit lands. Player-only on purpose: mobs already size their survivability from mob_HP, so giving them a second pool would count the same anchor twice (checks.md H1). Hits of every Element, including chaos, and burn DoT drain Energy Shield before HP; poison and bleed DoT bypass it. Armour + Elemental resistance shrink the hit that drains it.

evasion_roll.note: The first opening_rating Evasion points count at opening_share; points above that count at earned_mult. The effective rating is opposed by attacker Accuracy and capped by caps.evasion. The opening chance stays below opening_max_chance_pct even against the least accurate zone-1 lineage, while preserving the value of Agi and gear in later zones. Mob Evasion and outgoing hit chance keep their own accuracy-versus-rating roll.

caps.block_note: `block` is the second avoidance layer: a blocked hit is cut by a flat `armour / 10` (owner ruling, provisional) rather than deleted, and the roll runs after perfect dodge and evasion. It is fed by the Shield offhand's line 1 only. **No Cap (owner ruling):** the block chance keeps climbing with the shield's own Mod line. formula-defense.md prints the order.
caps.stun_note: `stun` is the lightning stun chance (elements.md lightning · C10): `Alignment × K_STUN_PER_ALIGN` plus the `Chance to stun %` gear line. **No Cap (owner ruling):** the two sources sum and the chance keeps climbing; the mace's line 1 is the published gear source.
caps.notes: `evasion` is the one avoidance Cap (80) and AGI carries it (owner ruling): the rating is `agi x K_EVASION` with the `evasion_flat` / `evasion_pct` gear lines riding on the same rating, so Dex no longer feeds it at all. The opening-weighted effective rating in `evasion_roll` runs the opposed roll and the Cap binds against the low-accuracy lineages, which is what C1/C2 and X20 prove. **No Cap (owner ruling):** `perfect_dodge`, `block`, `stun` and `alignment` are all open-ended. Perfect dodge is not opposed and deletes the hit outright, so it binds on the Lck ratio alone and keeps climbing with it. **`elem_res` (75) and `cdr` (80) are hard ceilings, not build targets**: a maxed single-stat build reaches only 48.45 / 57.375, so each Cap sits above its own build by intent. `elem_res` is the one Cap with an unlock: a passive-tree node raises the ceiling, and the engine takes that raise as the `capBonus` its `resistanceOf` argument carries. `elem_res_max` is that unlocked ceiling and its only home, and `resistanceOf` clamps `elem_res + capBonus` there however the raise is stacked — T9 proves the tree's fully-bought node lands exactly on it. `attack_interval_sec` is the clock Cap in its own unit (owner ruling): `hits_per_sec` never passes `1 / attack_interval_sec`, whatever the weapon, because a percent ceiling let a dagger clock faster than a staff. The engine derives its `aspd` ceiling from that one number. **X11** proves the split: a build-target Cap must have reach >= cap (it must bind), a hard-ceiling Cap must have reach <= cap (it must not).

weapon_size_mult.bolt_note: A magic weapon has no swing, it has a bolt: a press on the attack clock with no mana and no cooldown, worth this share of the finished hit so the filler is never a downgrade on a full swing (X50). It used to be derived from the attack roster weakest stated percentage; a press is no longer a percentage of a hit (it is its own flat plus an effectiveness), so the bolt own share lives here.
weapon_size_mult.note: Weapon x body class (HugePatch section 12): the shape of a fight, not a stat. One multiplier on the PHYSICAL share of an outgoing hit, applied after mitigation, so it never scales the armour cut; the weapon's own swing always carries its row (a staff's swing included), a physical attack skill carries it too, and a magic-damage skill is exempt. Three columns, not four: a boss is not a size, it declares which column it reads (mob.sizes[].reads_as, overridable per boss). The one-handed sword is the flat reference row, which is what keeps every zone price still. One-handed axe remains at neutral 1.0 for all sizes pending a balance decision. Every row keys a weapon NAME from bases.json `weapons`; other flat rows remain uncalibrated until decided.

herbs.note: A herb bundle drops on its own roll, separate from gear and stones. farm.md prints these; F13 in checks.md is generated from here.

farm.note: Settlement Farming is the herb-provisioning life skill: plant a seed on a plot, wait the growth timer, harvest for Farming XP plus herbs. It remains separate from the field skills (Mining, Woodcutting, Hunting and Cooking). Farm and field-skill XP are independent of character XP and do not alter mob_HP.

abandoned-camp.name: Abandoned Camp
abandoned-camp.description: A sheltered fire pit and fresh water. Restore Hunger once before this camp disappears.

provision-caravan.name: Provision Caravan
provision-caravan.description: Travelers offer a bundle of the region's provisions. Collect it once before the caravan leaves.

fieldwork.note: Field life skills follow a prepare-travel-hunt-cook loop. Configured skill-level milestones increase harvest amounts; skill level and per-resource Mastery improve field-material and provision drop rates within a cap, without changing gear or stone drops. Hunger drains on walks, hunts and gathering. Raw food, fruit, edible herbs and cooked dishes have distinct uses. Humans can carry cooked rations, goblins scavenge raw haunches, and wild creatures yield local forage. Empty Hunger cuts HP regeneration by the configured amount and never touches Energy Shield recharge. Road events are an independent supply/rest roll per crossed block and do not spawn a road mob group. Trail sites are authored per settlement and scale with its band — one in low, two in mid, three in high — each on its own bare block outside any named side, and a settlement with no spare bare block keeps the one it has. All rates and effects live here; map.json remains presentation only. Regional Mine and Grove bonus yields are authored per zone in regional_sources. Existing ore, timber and rarewood keep their keys and uses. Workshop recipes consume gathered materials at a settlement and produce trade goods; all cooking recipes also define edible cooked provisions.

events.text: Found wild berries along the trail
Found a cache of forest nuts
Found field mushrooms beneath a fallen log
A sunroot breaks through the roadside earth
Moonmint glimmers in the trail shade
A clear spring restores your strength

camp.note: The first field Camp and its first relocation are free, so the player can reach both gathering sites. Later relocations consume ore and timber. A Camp is safe ground and the field Push return point for its zone.

potions.note: Single home for the potion ladder farm.md prints (A8). Effect is % of the relevant pool, applied instantly; the value is derived as base + step × tier_index (HP tiers 1-3 → 10/20/30 · mana tiers 1-3 → 15/25/35). Potions are provisioning, not power: they are suppressed on bosses (combat.md §7), sit on a shared cooldown, are capped per fight, and almost never trigger inside a 1-sec AFK farm kill — so they do NOT enter the survival model (tools/survival.ts) and move no mob_HP · drop line · timeline number (H1). The 2026-10-03 survival re-run (SV1-SV5 green) confirms they remain a bounded non-combat convenience — this closes the old 'pending survival rerun' note.

presets.note: Loadout presets (`skill-pool.md` Preset · `skill-pool-system.md` rule 12 · save.md Skills). Six sets can be stored; the game selects one automatically by zone, and a Push returns the player to the main preset while cooldowns already counting keep counting. The count and the reset rule live here so the client and the docs read one number.

skill_drop.note: A skill piece is its own drop stream, separate from gear and stones. Rates are per kill and are the only place they are written; skill-pool-system.md prints them.

skill_xp.note: Skill level is earned the PoE way: every kill awards 1 XP to each skill that is in the list (attack, curse, heal) or open (aura) at that moment, and 400 XP buys one step up to the Cap of 20. So maxing one skill takes 7,600 kills of using it (loot.md section 2) - and it never depends on how often the skill happened to fire, on mana, or on list length. This replaces the old cube-root curve, which needed ~6.86M presses to reach 20 and was therefore unreachable.

build.reference_split: Str 12 items · Agi/Lck/Dex at level-only 210 · sword (aspd 1.2 · mult 1.0) · main hand T1 aspd +25% · crit damage +120%
build.weapon_aspd_default_note: The aspd a build with no weapon in hand clocks at (the bare-hand fallback). It is the sword's own `weapon_aspd` in bases.json, read from here so the empty slot and the opening set cannot drift apart.
build.hit_chance_pct_note: A derived anchor, not an input: the engine's own REFERENCE build hit chance against the reference mob (mean species on a Medium body), rounded. X21 gates it exact, and `node tools/check.ts --sync` re-publishes it here whenever a K, a Cap, a species Dex line or a body top-up moves - the gate stays exact so a stale figure cannot survive, and the repair is one command instead of a hand-typed number.
build.heal_pool_mult_note: One round of the heal skills, as a multiple of Max HP: Greater Heal 60% + Heal 10%/sec x 8 sec (80%) = 140% => x2.40. Read by tools/survival.ts for the boss 'with heal' column; the heal skills in skills.json must sum to this number. Retuned from x2.09 when the survival cage's weapon was corrected to the one-handed sword (the old dagger was 25% too fast, so every boss Push was understated): at x2.40 one round still clears the boss for the two themes that spend items on surviving (mix, tank) and not for glass or evasion.

global.note: The two umbrella multipliers reserved for future sources. `global damage` multiplies outgoing damage once, after weak / Element counter / crit; `global defend` is the incoming step-7 `damage_taken_mult` bucket (combat.md section 2). Both start at x1.00 and no source grants either yet — a future skill or aura feeds one bucket, so the two never stack as separate multipliers. `global speed` (Haste) is the third reserved term: it scales the whole clock (cooldowns and final attack speed). **Player-only:** global speed affects the player alone and no mob ever carries Haste, even when mobs get their own skill lists.

variant_lean.note: A variant's lean tilts the three collectible streams — gear, herbs, junk — toward one of them by redistributing probability mass, never raising the total expected drops/kill, so the drop line and the timeline stay put. The variant row owns it (`mob.variant_drops` `lean`) and nothing overrides it: the player used to have a per-zone Hunt Order on top, and that control is gone. Stones ride the elite/boss lines and are not a category. 'none' is the identity, so a variant that carries none behaves exactly as the balanced case.

filter.note: The bag filter keeps a drop only when it beats the equipped piece in the same slot by more than noise. Scored as Sum(weight(line) x value / Total), a swap must gain at least upgrade_margin_pct, because a 2% gain is not a decision - it is a reroll. tools/loot.ts measures the keep-rates that margin produces and loot.md publishes them; game/src/sim/gear/filter.ts reads the same value as the per-slot default, so a raised threshold is a player setting and never a second number.

rules.note: loot.md section 4 names the configurable conditions: the upgrade margin and keep Elemental res of an Element the player lacks. They are stored per slot (save.md) and start equal for every slot. The filter is OFF by default: a fresh character keeps every gear drop and dissolves nothing, so the player turns the filter on per slot and sets the thresholds; only then does a piece that fails its slot rule produce the complete salvage resource bundle. Value stones come later from settlement Alchemy, and stones are always kept. The old keep-only-Rare condition died with Rarity: an item's level is a continuous number now, so 'better than what I wear' is the whole question.

frame_mod.note: Line 1 of every item (the Frame Mod). An armour frame names the FLAT defence lines it carries - one, two or all three of Armour flat, Evasion flat and Energy Shield flat, the seven non-empty combinations whose complete set each armour slot's frames carry without repeating one (owner ruling: the frame name says which, and the Frame Mod is flat only). A multi-line Frame Mod shares one budget, so `value_scale` is what each Mod on the line is multiplied by once the count is known: 100% alone, 70% with a partner, 55% with two, so a wider line is worth having but never free. Weapons force every Mod their parenthesised list names; an off-hand frame carries its family's row; belt / ring / amulet / earring roll line 1 from the slot's own pool. `bases.json` owns the frame lists; this block owns only the scale.

quality_stone_sources.note: crafting.md prices the +1..+15 ladder as 1/2/3/4/5 · 7/9/11/13/15 · 18/21/24/27/30 Quality stones and says the source shifts monsters → elites → bosses by step (steps 1-5 · 6-10 · 11-15). These are the income side of that same split: the per-kill figures and the kills a full 12-piece set takes are derived from them (checks.md F20-F22), never typed beside them.

repair_stone_sources.note: crafting.md: Repair stone comes from elites and bosses only, one per revive.

corrupt_stone_sources.note: crafting.md: Corrupt stone is boss only and the rarest stone, one use per piece.

replace_stone_sources.note: The Replace stone trades the Add stone’s identity roll for the player’s own choice. It charges one stone like every press — what makes it the dearer purchase is where it comes from, not how many stones one press eats: it is gated one step tighter than Add on the same Elite/Boss split, half the Add stone’s Elite chance, and a Boss pays one on half its chance so a Boss is still not a guaranteed replacement.

imprint_stone_sources.note: One stone per eligible gear Mod (imprint_<id>): it names one Unbound line and rewrites it as its own Mod, rolling Tier and value fresh. Elites pay one random imprint stone on their own chance; a Boss pays two. The Mod is uniform over the eligible roster declared in mods.json; passive-tree-only Mods are excluded, while eligible Mods outside a Base's ordinary pool remain available.

polish_stone_sources.note: The Polish stone edits every line where a Replace stone edits one, and the Frame Mod and Bound pair it reaches are lines no other stone can edit at any price, so it is gated one step tighter than Replace on the Elite half and keeps Replace's Boss half: half the Replace stone's Elite chance, and a Boss pays one on half its chance. The per-line Reroll stays the cheap path for the Unbound lines — this stone buys the three lines that are part of the piece, in one press.

reforge_stone_sources.note: The Reforge stone is the Corrupt stone's safer cousin — it redraws the piece's Tier instead of rolling a one-way table — but unlike Corrupt it leaves the piece open to every other stone, so a press is repeatable and it pays half the Corrupt stone's Boss chance. Bosses only: the gamble is on the whole piece, and an Elite should not hand one out.

rebirth_stone_sources.status: provisional · owner-veto-able · the chance is the boss-half ladder read one step further (Corrupt 0.25 · Reforge half = 0.125 · Rebirth half again = 0.0625), not a figure the sim has had to earn yet
rebirth_stone_sources.note: The Rebirth stone redraws the identity of every Unbound line the piece holds — the set the player was dealt, plus any line an Add stone filled — in one press. Frame Mod and Bound pair are untouched, the line count never moves, no Add charge is spent, and each redrawn Mod is the piece's own pool draw. Bosses only: a press re-opens a whole piece, and an Elite should not hand that out.

loot.unique_chance_note: Wild-unique rate: share of normal spawns upgraded to one of the Species' optional Uniques (mob.uniques).

road.note: Travel is walking. The world is a pointy-top hex lattice and a settlement owns its own hex; any cell may be stood on, so a walk joins the two cells it starts and ends on and is a count of blocks and never a link with a price. Every block costs `block_sec`; a walk is a transition to the destination field, which owns its spawn-slot population. There is no separate road encounter group, purse, chest or Standing. Gold and junk come from killing mobs, so walking can never mint (`economy.md`). A settlement's Waypoint unlocks the first time the character arrives there on foot, and then warps to any unlocked settlement instantly, for gold at the destination's band; a Waystone will be a second destination kind on the same rule. The Road's old ladder and branch links, its trip minutes, its terrain tilt table, its encounter kinds, the purse, the chest, the Circuit and the Standing-per-leg are all gone with this shape, and none of them comes back: a branch link has no meaning when the block count IS the distance - a pass would need its own shorter hex path in the lattice.
road.graph_rule: A node is one settlement's own hex in axial coordinates on the pointy-top lattice, which is the field the sheet draws: 20 columns by 15 rows, 300 cells, the starting settlement at the centre cell and the level bands climbing outward by distance rank. Blocks between two cells are their hex distance, computed from those coordinates and never typed, so a walk's length is derived and one block is one cell the player can see. Every cell is walkable from every other - there is no edge list, no route to buy and no ground that refuses a foot - and a walk to a far cell is plotted as an ordered chain of adjacent cells and crossed one cell at a time. A step only ever enters a cell adjacent to the one the foot is on, which is what makes the chain a walk and not a jump. A Waypoint covers the distance for gold once the settlement at the far end has been walked to.
road.standing_rule: Every cell of the field is a place to stand. A cell's zone is its nearest settlement's, measured in blocks and never typed; ground equally near two settlements belongs to the tied one holding the lowest zone, so a tie is answered by the rule and not by a coin toss. Rank is the distance from that settlement: 0 is the settlement itself, 1 is one of its sides, 2 and out is bare ground. Standing on a side that has a sub-zone written into it hunts that sub-zone's cast; standing where no sub-zone is named - in a town, on a side with nothing written into it, on bare ground - rolls the zone's whole cast. A Waypoint opens only where a cell is rank 0, because a Waypoint marks a settlement and not a patch of ground.
road.cost_rule: Every cell costs one block whatever lies under it: no terrain cost, no passability table, no ground dearer to cross than any other. A walk's price is the hex distance between its two cells times `block_sec`, so two routes of the same length are the same walk.
road.encounter_rule: A walk joins two cells; it rolls no separate road encounter group. The destination field owns its authored spawn-slot population, which is the only source of mobs and the ordinary drop roll. A block that rolls nothing stays silent.
road.push_rule: A Push costs recovery time. A same-zone Field Camp receives the character and ends the current walk without refunding a block. With no same-zone Field Camp, the existing walk is preserved and resumes on the interrupted block after recovery. Away time never walks.
road.waypoint_rule: Arriving at a settlement on foot unlocks its Waypoint, once. A Waypoint warps to any unlocked settlement instantly, and it costs gold at the destination settlement's own band: a warp buys back the walk's time, which is what gold is for, and it buys nothing else (`town.json` `waypoint_warp`). It never gates a zone: a settlement you have not walked to is reached by walking, and no amount of gold opens a Waypoint you have not earned on foot. A Waystone will be a second destination kind that a Waypoint may also target.

dungeon.note: One dungeon per zone, on the first wild side of its settlement (map.json). A run is a mode, not a place: the sim never reads a coordinate (M7), it only knows whether a run is open. A run fields mob_cap normal mobs of the zone it was entered in at that zone's own group sizes clamped to group_cap, and it pays the ordinary per-kill roll — the escrow only delays it, so mob_HP, the drop line and the timeline never move (D1). Loot waits in escrow until the last mob falls; a Push ends the run at once and the escrow is forfeited, never paid. A cleared run cools down for cooldown_sec before the next entry. Owner override: the timer and the forfeit are the veto-able exception to the clock rule.

inventory.note: One bag = 100 fixed slots. A kept gear piece takes one slot and a consumable stack takes one, and both are counted against the same 100. Stones and junk stack 999/slot and are weightless; herbs, potions, materials and provisions stack 100/slot and weigh 0.1/unit; gold takes no slot. Full = pickups pause: nothing auto-converts and nothing is deleted. Weight capacity is Str x K_STR_WEIGHT over everything carried, so a full bag can cut aspd up to -50% (formula.md section 11). Gear crafting and Stash are Settlement-only; Camp cooking is the field exception. The Stash is one warehouse on the character and every settlement's counter opens the same one, never a second chest per town. Every drop enters the bag by default; only a slot whose filter is armed dissolves a piece, which is what replaced the auto-convert buffer - kept gear fills at the measured upgrade rate (F4), not at the junk flow.

item_level.note: The one axis an item's strength rides (item-level.md). The value a Mod line rolls is a window that climbs with the item's level: the window's floor climbs from the band below (so a mid-band piece starts able to roll the low band's floor and ends above it), the ceiling is the band's own top, and the roll lands in one of the window's thirds - the top third is the rarest, so a high-level drop is a chance and not a formality. The Unbound line count is not on that ladder: it is drawn inside `unbound_slots` at drop, so two pieces of one level and one band can still differ in width.
item_level.span_note: The spans are the first loop's own level ranges - what the zone labels already say (low zones read 1-30, mid 31-60, high 61-90). A level past its band's span clamps to the band's own range, which is what keeps the later loops honest: a low-band zone at level 91 drops a low-band piece at the top of the low window, exactly as the zone label intends.
item_level.ascend_note: Ascend raises the piece one band and shifts its level by one span, so the window moves up a band without re-rolling the line - the same move the old quality step made, now expressed on the level. The value equals a span's length and is gated against it.
item_level.skeleton_note: Every item is line 1 the Frame Mod (unremovable, part of the frame) + 2 Bound lines (unremovable) + the Unbound lines it drew at drop (`unbound_slots`, 2 to 5), so a fresh drop carries 5-8 lines and the unremovable head is 3 of them. Each of the `mods_added_cap` Add stones fills one more Unbound line, which is what sets `crafted_max` = frame_mod_slots + bound_slots + unbound_slots.max + mods_added_cap, and a Unbound line never appears twice on one piece. `frame_mod_slots` is the unremovable floor's other half - the craft verbs refuse index < frame_mod_slots + bound_slots.

salvage.note: Each successfully dissolved gear piece produces the entire resource bundle. Immediate settlement Alchemy converts scrap into Value stones; only successfully produced Value units advance the Tier milestone. Expected income assumes rejected non-upgrade gear can be carried and processed, not guaranteed banked rewards.

save.note: save.md item 5: 3 walking snapshots guarding file corruption only, never wrong decisions (item 3). Triggers are level up, a successful Ascend or Refine, and every 10 minutes of play. A restore rewinds the whole account, so the shared Mastery is rebuilt from the surviving slot files rather than kept from after the craft.

junk.note: RO-style mob junk: a fourth drop stream, sold to the Settlement Counterhand for gold. `mob.variant_drops` owns each Variant's base item, rarity and lean; `mob.species[].junk_items` may add an alternate item in any selected rarity. A successful rarity roll pays the Variant item or its Species alternative when present at the Variant's rarity price, so each rarity's drop_chance_per_kill remains junk_per_kill / sell_gold and a kill keeps the reference base gold line (F3). Variant rarity buys drop frequency at a flat expected base value: common junk is frequent and cheap, rare junk is rare and dear, and the expected value is flat - which is also the bag-pressure trade. Junk stacks 999/slot and is weightless (like stones), so it fills bag slots and drives Settlement trips without a weight tax. The Counterhand buys this junk at its town demand quote alongside gathered materials, provisions and herbs; walking itself pays no gold - the old 'sell a rejected gear piece for 1 gold' option is retired.

aoe.note: Live area skills select all enemy centers inside the radius stored in skills.json, without a target-count cap. The primary receives the full press; additional targets receive per_target_pct of the press. A press pays its typed cost whether it lands on one target or many; target_cap describes the offline queue approximation, which has no spatial positions.

max_hp_press.note: Earth Splitter's share of the target's OWN maximum pool: the row states the percent, and a boss answers it at `boss_pct` of that (owner ticket). A press that scales with the body it lands on is priced by nothing in the archetype bands — the bands read the caster's power — so the row is priced on its own press and this cut is what keeps a %HP slam from out-punching the static `mob_HP` table every other number is priced against.

craft.roll_note: What one roll costs in Tier stones. Randomize redraws the Tier of the Mod a line holds; Reroll mod redraws the Mod itself and lands wherever the piece's own pool and weights put it. A bulk press pays this same figure times the lines it edits, so no number is typed beside it. The chosen swap above is dearer on purpose: the roll gambles, the swap does not.
craft.rebirth_note: One Rebirth stone buys one press, and the press is the whole Unbound set: every line the piece holds past the Bound pair — including any line an Add stone filled — leaves and a fresh Mod is drawn in its place from the piece's own pool. It is priced as one press rather than one stone a line because the reach is the product: the player is not choosing any of the five lines, only taking the set again. The Frame Mod and the Bound pair are untouched, the line count never moves, no Add charge is spent, and each slot's Reroll floor leaves with the identity it held.
craft.polish_note: The Polish stone spends the Reroll rule across the whole piece in one press: every line's value re-rolls inside its own Tier, never below the floor that slot has ever held, and no Tier moves. It is the one stone the owner opened onto the unremovable head — the Frame Mod (line 1, on its shared `frame_mod.value_scale` budget) and the Bound pair are re-rolled with the Unbound lines — and it removes no line, spends no Add charge, moves no identity and no Element. A stone that buys reach, not a cheaper climb: the per-line Reroll is still the cheap path for the Unbound lines, and only this one reaches the three lines that are part of the piece.
craft.reforge_note: The Reforge stone redraws the piece's Tier the way a drop does — one draw on the published weights, spent on the whole piece at once — then rolls every line's value inside the Tier it landed on, the Frame Mod on its shared budget. So it can climb every line together or drag them down: the Tier is the gamble and the values follow it. Identity, Element, line count and the Add charge are untouched. A slot whose Tier moved loses its Reroll floor, because a floor is the highest value that line held at that Tier; a slot the draw left where it was keeps its floor.
craft.imprint_note: The Imprint stone carries one eligible gear Mod's identity (imprint_<id>): it names one Unbound line and rewrites it as that Mod, rolling Tier and value fresh the way a drop does, even outside the Base's ordinary pool. Eligibility lives in mods.json. Passive-tree-only Mods cannot be Imprinted; legacy stones and item lines keep their saved identities and counts. One stone a use. It never touches the Frame Mod or the Bound pair, spends no Add charge and changes no line count.
craft.replace_note: The Replace stone spends what Remove + Add spend (1 + 1): it names the line that leaves and the line that comes in from the piece's own pool, and it rolls the incoming line's Tier fresh - the Mod's identity stops being a gamble, the Tier stays one, so a chosen line still has to be climbed with Reroll tier. It never touches the Frame Mod or the Bound pair, spends no Add charge and changes no line count.
craft.gear_mod_note: One Upgrade step adds this to the piece's Gear Mod, whose school is set by its Base and not rolled (item-base.md). The bound is the published line ceiling: `tools/loot.ts` rolls that same line off `mod_max`, so a full +15 ladder may not pass the smallest of the three school ceilings — `evasion_flat_t1` 30 ÷ `craft.upgrade_cap` 15 = 2. At +15 a light piece therefore reaches its whole T1 Evasion line, a heavy piece three quarters of the Armour 40 line and a cloth piece half of Energy Shield 60. checks.md H1 pays for the uplift against the boss now that measured `mob_HP` is already inside the pacing (it moves nothing there).
craft.corrupt_note: crafting.md's own Vaal table, copied: 25% nothing · 20% reroll values inside the current Tiers · 15% +1 Mod (crafted max and Core slot cap respected) · 15% remove one non-bound Mod · 10% reroll Element (the only Element change in the game) · 10% Gear Mod +2 · 5% one Item quality step down. One use per piece, and a corrupted piece accepts no further stones of any kind.
craft.upgrade_note: crafting.md's ladder, copied: +1 to +4 safe · +5 to +10 90% down to 45% and a fail drops one level with its Gear Mod points · +11 to +15 40% down to 10% and a fail breaks the piece · protection 5 per piece from birth, each would-be break spends one and drops a level · Repair stone revives one upgrade level below the pre-break level and refills protection · costs 1/2/3/4/5 then 7/9/11/13/15 then 18/21/24/27/30 Quality stones · online only

forge.note: Material-driven gear creation. A pattern names the slot or weapon type; the chosen material's family picks the Base/Frame and its grade sets the item band. The output is rolled with the drop skeleton (line 1 + Bound pair + Unbound lines), then behaves like any other piece. No gold fee; pattern.count is the material cost. Fancier Base variants stay drop-only.

f_rows_carried.value: first 1/14 of drops 21.9 → 2/14-4/14 10.5 → after that 6.2 (low band) · keep-rate 5.21% low · 4.05% mid · 3.00% high · 1.04% high + full_lck
f_rows_carried.expression: measured — tools/loot.ts, the seven roll steps in loot.md section 1

f_rows_carried.value: 0.34 Flat lines per high-zone drop (6.44 lines per item) · the four early-game Flats thin out as Item quality rises
f_rows_carried.expression: Flat line per drop (high zone, after the 0.25 early-game weighting)
skill per 1,000 kills · skill-pool.md drop chances

f_rows_carried.value: max 3 uses per fight · 30 sec shared cooldown · suppressed on bosses
Tier milestones derive from eligible Scrap Alchemy Value production
f_rows_carried.expression: Value income / salvage.alchemy.outputs_per_tier_stone; included once in Tier income

elements.note: 6 Elements. No Element counters another: a hit Element names its status and answers the target resistance line, nothing more. Earth keeps its own status (`crippled`, the clock cut) and is still waiting on its attack rows, so `pending` names it and it rolls on gear, takes a colour and meets the resistance Cap meanwhile. Each Species attacks with one Element and authors its own `mob.species[].resistance` and `mob.species[].weakness`; the two are separate lines. The same Cap the player obeys holds every resistance.

pending.earth: the element's status (`crippled`) is live; its attack rows land in a later pass. Gear can roll it and the Cap answers it meanwhile.

elements.colour_note: The damage indicator's one colour set (`hud`): a hit is coloured by the Element that carried it, a physical hit by `physical`, and a status proc by the colour of the Element its `status_of` line names, so no status needs its own copy of a colour. Crit is not an Element and takes the HUD's own accent, `--gold`.

opening.note: Minute one. Everything the game hands the player before they touch anything, so a client can create a playable character from one read. The player starts wearing nothing and pockets the `potions` kit - one draught per pool - so the first fight is survivable by drinking, not by free frames. The `gear` set below is the hand-authored reference set the OP gates still shape-check (one line per slot, floor Frame Mod, no Bound pair); it is not worn until the owner reopens starting gear. Every line is derived by the client, never typed here - `openingGear()` calls the same `loot.frameModAtFloor` a pre-skeleton save restore uses - so the frame per slot is the data's whole job and no number can drift.
opening.gear_note: The whole set, one piece per slot, and the lightest frame of every slot: it dresses the character at minute one without handing over a point of attack power. The frames' Frame Mods are defence and utility only (Energy Shield %, Max HP flat, Evasion %, Elemental alignment %, Block %) and the one weapon pair is the sword's own floor line, so the priced clock - mob_HP, the drop line, the timeline, the XP ladder - cannot move. The off hand is a Buckler on purpose: a Grimoire's Frame Mod is Magic power flat, which is attack power the curve does not pay for.
opening.gear_rule: main hand names a weapon TYPE (what a drop records as its base); every other slot names a Base frame from bases.json. The order here is the hand's own listing, not the SLOTS order - a client places each piece at its own slot, and the two ring entries take the two ring slots.
opening.skills_note: No starting skill on purpose. The mob-health curve gives a level-1 character 0.3% skill power, so a free attack skill would hand out several times what the mobs are priced against. The first skill is the first boss drop, which is also the first time the skill axis becomes visible.

first_rule.objective: the Guild's first Elite task, in the opening zone
first_rule.why: the task board already exists and pays stones only, so the first instruction costs no new system and no power outside the loot funnel - its reward sits inside the task income bound tasks.md already sets. It is an Elite hunt because the board's plain kill-count task is gone; the count and the payout are the board's own elite sizing, so nothing is typed twice
first_rule.completes_on: the first Elite task of the opening zone (the board's own elite sizing)
first_rule.reward: the standard elite payout (Tier stones), unmodified
first_rule.exit: once the first gear drop lands the task board stops being the tutorial and the player moves to the zone loop

opening.no_death: the player cannot be killed by the opening: zone-1 mobs take minutes to kill a level-1 character, and Push returns them to camp at full HP
